questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror should be positioned to show:

options.text: The rear tires.
All students on the bus.
The floor of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the overhead mirror to show the top of the rear window. This lets you see all students on the bus, including those sitting directly behind you.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Lock up your wheels.
Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Bus stops may be changed by:

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: The school district establishes all bus routes and stops. Drivers cannot change a stop location without written approval from a district official.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the right side of a bus.
On the steering wheel of a bus.
Above the windshield inside a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside a bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: During the driving test, when crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you must drive during high winds, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: A school bus can be pushed by wind. In windy conditions, grip the steering wheel firmly, expect wind gusts, and slow down. Contact your dispatcher if needed.

questions.question: During a vehicle control skills test, your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: In the general area described by the examiner.
In the exact final position described by the examiner.
Within three feet of the final position described by the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact final position described by the examiner.
questions.explanation: Finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. Not following instructions exactly can result in failing the skills test.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How well-spoken you are.
How quickly you arrive at your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior. Drive safely and responsibly, obey all traffic laws, and avoid accidents or violations.

questions.question: Outside mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: Before a trip begins.
While you are driving.
After students get on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before a trip begins.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving the bus.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus due to a hazard, a driver should:

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Explain the situation to the dispatcher.
Take time deciding if an evacuation is necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain the situation to the dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If time allows, contact your dispatcher before evacuating. Make evacuation decisions quickly when needed.

questions.question: Loading and unloading students from a bus:

options.text: Is simple and does not need supervision.
Can be dangerous and must be supervised.
Can be done without the bus driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous and must be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Bus drivers must follow safety procedures during these times. Loading and unloading must always be supervised.

questions.question: If a bus must be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Always use the rear door.
Use the safest exit available.
Always use the front door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest exit available.
questions.explanation: The driver must quickly decide which exit is safest for passengers to use during an evacuation.

questions.question: Student safety is best maintained by:

options.text: Keeping students on the bus.
Letting some students leave the bus.
Letting students leave the bus and scatter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest and easiest to control if they stay on the bus. Students should remain on the bus unless staying creates a risk of injury.

questions.question: If a student has a back injury, you should:

options.text: Move them off the bus.
Not move them.
Have them try to stand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not move them.
questions.explanation: Do not move a student with a neck or spine injury unless their life is in immediate danger.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, check the fifth wheel by:

options.text: Making sure the locking jaws are open.
Making sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Making sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed tightly around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: If your ABS is not working:

options.text: You will have no brakes at all.
You will still have brakes.
You should only use the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent wheels from locking during hard braking. If the ABS fails, your regular brakes will still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: When boarding a bus, students should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only when all other seats are full.
Sit as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only when all other seats are full.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Sitting toward the front is safer in a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: If a student drops something while approaching a bus, the student should:

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: If a student bends down to pick up an object, the driver cannot see them. This is dangerous. Students should move to a safe spot, get the driver's attention, and let the driver retrieve the dropped item.

questions.question: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors let you see all of the following, except:

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors should show the area in front of the bus from the bumper to where you can see directly. They should also show the front tires and the area from the front to the service door.

questions.question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you begin driving.
